limitations: shared_primitive_kinds is 16 (< 17) until at least one known-duplicate migration (wave 2: B/C/F) lands; the allow-list expires 2027-03-31 and the check then fails again.
The event log is not bounded (linear, as any exact record); SQLite stores payloads > 2 KiB compressed, Postgres (JSON columns) does not.

Retention drops only blobs a module declares superseded (today: the population's replaced neural checkpoints); every other blob is only packed. Checkpoints rooted by retained snapshots are kept (default keep_last=3 + one per 30 days), so checkpoint bytes still grow with the number of retained monthly snapshots.
The state keeps one `artifacts` metadata row per system array blob (36.8k rows after 30 days, about 450k after 365 days): snapshot size grows with it.

Main-line isolation covers same-transaction subscribers. Couplings implemented as scheduled processes, or sharing kernel counters (unkeyed sched job ids), still shift later main-line positions; appliers that store an event's absolute seq in state (4.0 search_docs.seq) differ in that field when side events exist.

Event.via and main-line keying change the hashes of every world with subscribers or typed validation (v5 content/community worlds, typed worlds); 4.0 worlds stay byte-identical (tests/test_v5_substrate_kernel.py goldens). The boot.py line-counting change changes the recorded cost of failing sandboxed requests, so v5 population/sandbox world hashes differ from earlier recorded runs.

Fault injection reached 58 scheduled jobs but only 2 agent commands (random schema-valid commands rarely span modules) and 1 subscriber cascade; deliberate composed failures come from a test driver module (labelled as such).
Cross-process exactness is verified on this machine (CPU torch), not across machines.
Warm-worker effects other than traceback formatting (e.g. program-level caches in sandboxed services) could still make a resumed world differ; none observed in the tested worlds.
Mode B and Mode C are not operational: no domain registers environments, no civ provider exists.

Bytes uploaded through the artifact.put tool are also in the recorded cmd event (arguments are recorded for regeneration); module code should store large media with artifacts.put, whose events hold only the REF.
A world moved to another store must run artifacts.export(world, dest_store) before it is loaded in another process.
At the start of this session I deleted two audit probe databases (scratchpad/audit/A_J_substrate_civ/resume.sqlite, resume2.sqlite) to save disk; the audit's recorded numbers are unaffected.

Mandatory duplicate-fact check: any NEW table, column table or column whose name carries a shared-kind signature (facts.SIGNATURES) makes primitives.problems / check_no_duplicates fail until it is classified in substrate/facts.py REVIEWED (reviewed by A). Every workstream adding tables: send A the classification (owner/part/extension/private/duplicate).

Ownership decisions and migrations (facts.KNOWN_DUPLICATES, all expire 2027-03-31): B (+F/G/I/C): crowd, 4.0 consumers, patrons, npc_workers, society minds, labor_workers, sci_npc and adopt_people become views of `pop` individuals (D-15); pop.employer becomes a cache derived from employment contracts (B+F). C: relationship moves to social.cols:follow (forum.follow writes social edges, forum_follows retired); community moves to community.communities (forum boards become a community's discussion space); creator memberships and newsletter subscriptions become subs subscriptions (C+F); aud_item_info reads catalogue metadata instead of copying it (C+D). F: institution moves to inst.inst_charters (gov constitutions migrate), commitments become contracts with an escrow clause, xchg listings become market listings with an exchange venue, the 4.0 job board stays in 4.0 families (v5 hiring through labor -> employment contracts). J: 4.0 industry.offers become listings or stay 4.0-only. After a migration A changes OWNERS and removes the allow-list entry.

Mode C (J): a civ provider is operational only if its world passes modes.composition; modes.DOMAINS maps the 17 Part 2.1 domains to module names - J/I add their modules there (education currently: learn, kb; energy: make.grid* events, fleet).
Mode B (I): the domains provider lists 0 environments; domains must register configurations (crucible.domains.base) for Mode B to count.

Typed events: worlds with params.typed_events validate every registered type of their modules (incl. the 4.0 owner schemas); validators are passive subscribers and do not change the trajectory. bus.coverage(world) reports typed vs emitted types: other workstreams should register their event types (coverage was 11 of 77 in the audit).

Long runs (J, M): call retention.compact(world, prune=True) after periodic snapshots; history.state_at for historical queries; World.load for resume. In store-less multi-world processes call World.close() (or drop references) so pool bytes are released.
